question: For robots with over 1000 Total Operating Hours, analyze their maintenance priority level. Display each robot's ID, Weighted Fault Prediction Score value, Minimum Remaining Useful Life value, TOH, Number of Operations, and the Maintenance Priority Level. Sort results by WFPS in descending order and MRUL in ascending order, limiting to top 100 robots.
SQL: WITH fault_metrics AS ( SELECT upkeeprobot, SUM(faultpredscore * ( 1.0 / ( 1 + upkeepduedays ) )) / SUM(1.0 / ( 1 + upkeepduedays )) AS wfps, MIN(rulhours) AS mrul FROM maintenance_and_fault GROUP BY upkeeprobot ), operation_stress AS ( SELECT operbotdetref, MAX(totopshrval) AS toh, COUNT(*) AS operation_count FROM operation GROUP BY operbotdetref ) SELECT rd.botdetreg, fm.wfps, fm.mrul, os.toh, os.operation_count, CASE WHEN fm.wfps > 0.6 AND fm.mrul < 200 THEN 'CRITICAL' WHEN fm.wfps > 0.4 OR fm.mrul < 500 THEN 'WARNING' ELSE 'NORMAL' END AS maintenance_priority FROM robot_details AS rd JOIN fault_metrics AS fm ON rd.botdetreg = fm.upkeeprobot JOIN operation_stress AS os ON rd.botdetreg = os.operbotdetref WHERE os.toh > 1000 ORDER BY fm.wfps DESC NULLS FIRST, fm.mrul ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 100
evidence: Maintenance Priority Level: Classifies robots into maintenance priority categories based on fault prediction scores and remaining useful life, Weighted Fault Prediction Score (WFPS): Calculates a weighted average fault prediction score, prioritizing recent records., Minimum Remaining Useful Life (MRUL): Finds the minimum Remaining Useful Life across all maintenance records for a specific robot., Total Operating Hours (TOH): The maximum total operating hours recorded for the robot across all operations., Number of Operations (NO): Counts the number of operation records for a specific robot.

For each robot, display its ID, average tool wear percentage, TWR value, TPC value, average cycle time in seconds, and its tool replacement status. Show the top 100 robots ordered by tool wear rate (highest first) and then by total program cycles (highest first).
SQL: WITH tool_metrics AS ( SELECT effectivenessrobot, AVG(toolwearpct) AS avg_wear, SUM(toolwearpct) / NULLIF(SUM(tc.progcyclecount), 0) AS twr FROM performance_and_safety AS ps JOIN operation AS tc ON ps.effectivenessrobot = tc.operbotdetref GROUP BY effectivenessrobot ), cycle_metrics AS ( SELECT operbotdetref, SUM(progcyclecount) AS tpc, AVG(cycletimesecval) AS avg_cycle_time FROM operation GROUP BY operbotdetref ) SELECT rd.botdetreg, tm.avg_wear, tm.twr, cm.tpc, cm.avg_cycle_time, CASE WHEN tm.twr > 0.001 AND cm.tpc > 10000 THEN 'URGENT' WHEN tm.twr > 0.0005 OR tm.avg_wear > 75 THEN 'WARNING' ELSE 'NORMAL' END AS tool_status FROM robot_details AS rd JOIN tool_metrics AS tm ON rd.botdetreg = tm.effectivenessrobot JOIN cycle_metrics AS cm ON rd.botdetreg = cm.operbotdetref ORDER BY tm.twr DESC NULLS FIRST, cm.tpc DESC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 100
evidence: Average Cycle Time: Calculates the average time in seconds for completing one program cycle, Total Program Cycles (TPC): Sums the program cycle counts across all operations for a specific robot., Tool Wear Rate (TWR): Estimates the rate of tool wear relative to program cycles., Tool Replacement Status: Classifies robots into tool replacement priority categories based on tool wear rate and program cycles

question: Analyze robots' cycle efficiency category, where for each robot, show its ID, model series, OCE value, TPC value, average cycle time, number of unique programs, most recent cycle time, and efficiency category. Also, show each robot's efficiency ranking within its model series. Only include robots with over 100,000 program cycles. Show top 100 robots ordered by OCE (highest first) then by TPC.
SQL: WITH cycle_metrics AS ( SELECT o.operbotdetref, SUM(o.progcyclecount) as tpc, AVG(o.cycletimesecval) as avg_cycle_time, SUM(o.progcyclecount)*1.0/NULLIF(SUM(o.cycletimesecval), 0) as oce, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT o.currprogval) as unique_programs FROM operation o GROUP BY o.operbotdetref ), temporal_efficiency AS ( SELECT cm.operbotdetref, cm.oce, cm.tpc, cm.avg_cycle_time, LENGTH(cm.unique_programs) - LENGTH(REPLACE(cm.unique_programs, ',', '')) + 1 as program_count, FIRST_VALUE(o.cycletimesecval) OVER ( PARTITION BY o.operbotdetref ORDER BY rr.rects DESC ) as latest_cycle_time FROM cycle_metrics cm JOIN operation o ON cm.operbotdetref = o.operbotdetref JOIN robot_record rr ON o.operrecref = rr.recreg ) SELECT rd.botdetreg, rd.modelseriesval, te.oce, te.tpc, te.avg_cycle_time, te.program_count, te.latest_cycle_time, CASE WHEN te.oce < 100 AND te.tpc > 500000 THEN 'Low Efficiency' WHEN te.oce < 150 OR te.tpc > 300000 THEN 'Medium Efficiency' ELSE 'High Efficiency' END as efficiency_category, DENSE_RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY rd.modelseriesval ORDER BY te.oce DESC ) as efficiency_rank_in_model FROM robot_details rd JOIN temporal_efficiency te ON rd.botdetreg = te.operbotdetref WHERE te.tpc > 100000 ORDER BY te.oce DESC, te.tpc DESC LIMIT 100
evidence: Total Program Cycles (TPC): Sums the program cycle counts across all operations for a specific robot., Operation Cycle Efficiency (OCE): Calculates the efficiency of program cycles relative to cycle time., Average Cycle Time: Calculates the average time in seconds for completing one program cycle, Cycle Efficiency Category: Categorizes robots based on their program cycle efficiency performance

question: I want to analyze Energy Efficiency Ratio patterns for robots with Energy Inefficient Robot status across different application types. Please list each application type, the average EER, and the worst EER Rank. Sort the results by average EER from highest to lowest, and limit the output to 100 rows.
SQL: WITH inefficient_robots AS ( SELECT rd.botdetreg AS robot_id, op.apptypeval AS application_type, rd.modelseriesval AS model_series, SUM(ps.energyusekwhval) / MAX(op.totopshrval) AS eer FROM robot_details AS rd JOIN operation AS op ON rd.botdetreg = op.operbotdetref JOIN performance_and_safety AS ps ON rd.botdetreg = ps.effectivenessrobot GROUP BY rd.botdetreg, op.apptypeval, rd.modelseriesval HAVING SUM(ps.energyusekwhval) / MAX(op.totopshrval) > 0.01 AND MAX(op.totopshrval) > 1000 ), eer_ranks AS ( SELECT application_type, robot_id, eer, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY application_type ORDER BY eer DESC NULLS FIRST) AS eer_rank FROM inefficient_robots ) SELECT application_type, AVG(eer) AS average_eer, MAX(eer_rank) AS worst_eer_rank FROM eer_ranks GROUP BY application_type ORDER BY average_eer DESC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 100
evidence: Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER): Measures energy efficiency by comparing energy usage to operating hours., Energy Inefficient Robot: Flags robots with poor energy efficiency., Total Operating Hours (TOH): The maximum total operating hours recorded for the robot across all operations., EER Rank: Ranks the Energy Efficiency Ratio within each application type to assess relative efficiency.

question: I want to analyze robots with Precision Category of low and medium precision and High Fault Risk by controller type. Please list each controller type, the average Average Position Error, the maximum APE Rank, the average Recent Fault Prediction Score, and the number of robots. Only include robots with Robot Age in Years over 1 year. Sort by the maximum APE Rank from highest to lowest and limit to 50 rows.
SQL: WITH PositionError AS ( SELECT ad.actdetref, rd.ctrltypeval, AVG(ad.poserrmmval) AS ape FROM actuation_data ad JOIN robot_details rd ON ad.actdetref = rd.botdetreg GROUP BY ad.actdetref, rd.ctrltypeval ), FaultScore AS ( SELECT mf.upkeeprobot, MAX(mf.faultpredscore) AS rfps FROM maintenance_and_fault mf GROUP BY mf.upkeeprobot ), RobotAge AS ( SELECT rd.botdetreg, (JULIANDAY(rr.rects) - JULIANDAY(rd.instdateval)) / 365.25 AS ray FROM robot_details rd JOIN robot_record rr ON rd.botdetreg = rr.recreg ), Ranked AS ( SELECT pe.actdetref, pe.ctrltypeval, pe.ape, CAST(RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY pe.ctrltypeval ORDER BY pe.ape DESC) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY pe.ctrltypeval) AS ape_rank FROM PositionError pe ) SELECT r.ctrltypeval AS controller_type, AVG(r.ape) AS avg_ape, MAX(r.ape_rank) AS max_ape_rank, AVG(COALESCE(fs.rfps, 0)) AS avg_rfps, COUNT(DISTINCT r.actdetref) AS robot_count FROM Ranked r LEFT JOIN FaultScore fs ON r.actdetref = fs.upkeeprobot INNER JOIN RobotAge ra ON r.actdetref = ra.botdetreg WHERE r.ape >= 0.1 AND COALESCE(fs.rfps, 0) > 0.5 AND ra.ray > 1 GROUP BY r.ctrltypeval ORDER BY max_ape_rank DESC LIMIT 50
evidence: Average Position Error (APE): Calculates the average position error across all actuations for a specific robot., Recent Fault Prediction Score (RFPS): The fault prediction score from the most recent maintenance record for a robot., APE Rank: Ranks the Average Position Error within each controller type to assess relative precision., Precision Category: Categorizes the precision of the robot based on average position error., High Fault Risk: Indicates if the robot has a high risk of fault based on average fault prediction score., Robot Age in Years (RAY): Calculates the age of the robot in years based on installation date and record timestamp.

question: Show me how solar panel performance changes with age by calculating the Panel Performance Ratio (PPR) for different age groups. I want to see the panel age in years since installation, the average PPR and the number of panels of each age group. Sort the results from newest to oldest panels.
SQL: SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', pl.initdate) AS INTEGER) AS panel_age_years, AVG(pe.measpoww / p.powratew * 100) AS avg_ppr, COUNT(*) AS panel_count FROM panel p JOIN plant pl ON p.hubregistry = pl.growregistry JOIN performance pe ON p.panemark = pe.solmodref GROUP BY panel_age_years ORDER BY panel_age_years;
evidence: Panel Performance Ratio (PPR): Measures how well a solar panel is performing relative to its rated power.

question: Generate a prioritized maintenance list for solar plants by calculating Maintenance Return on Investment (MROI). The output must include: plant name, capacity in MW, total maintenance costs, revenue losses, maintenance cost efficiency score, revenue loss rate, MROI value and final priority level (URGENT/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) based on Maintenance Urgency Classification. Sort with most critical plants first, then by highest MROI.
SQL: SELECT p.growalias AS plant_name, p.gencapmw AS capacity_mw, SUM(m.maintcostusd) AS total_maintenance_costs, SUM(m.revlossusd) AS revenue_losses, AVG(m.maintcostusd / p.gencapmw) AS maintenance_cost_efficiency_score, AVG(m.revlossusd / p.gencapmw) AS revenue_loss_rate, AVG((m.revlossusd - m.maintcostusd) / p.gencapmw) AS mroi_value, CASE WHEN AVG((m.revlossusd - m.maintcostusd) / p.gencapmw) > 100 THEN 'URGENT' WHEN AVG((m.revlossusd - m.maintcostusd) / p.gencapmw) > 50 THEN 'HIGH' WHEN AVG((m.revlossusd - m.maintcostusd) / p.gencapmw) > 0 THEN 'MEDIUM' ELSE 'LOW' END AS final_priority_level FROM plant AS p LEFT JOIN maintenance AS m ON p.growregistry = m.powerref GROUP BY p.growalias, p.gencapmw ORDER BY CASE WHEN final_priority_level = 'URGENT' THEN 1 WHEN final_priority_level = 'HIGH' THEN 2 WHEN final_priority_level = 'MEDIUM' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END, mroi_value DESC;
evidence: Maintenance Return on Investment (MROI): Evaluates the financial return of maintenance activities., Maintenance Urgency Classification: Four-tier system prioritizing maintenance actions based on combined financial and operational factors, Maintenance Cost Efficiency (MCE): Evaluates the cost-effectiveness of maintenance relative to the plant's capacity., Revenue Loss Rate (RLR): Calculates the revenue loss per MW of capacity due to maintenance issues.

question: Analyze our solar plant maintenance effectiveness by calculating the Maintenance Return on Investment (MROI). Could you show me for each plant: its name, Maintenance Cost Efficiency, Revenue Loss Rate, and the resulting MROI score - so we can see which maintenance investments give the best returns?
SQL: WITH plant_maintenance_costs AS ( SELECT p.growalias, p.gencapmw, SUM(m.maintcostusd + m.cleancostusd + m.replacecostusd) AS total_maintenance_cost, AVG(m.revlossusd) AS avg_rev_loss FROM plant AS p JOIN maintenance AS m ON m.powerref = p.growregistry GROUP BY p.growalias, p.gencapmw ), maint_efficiency AS ( SELECT growalias, gencapmw, total_maintenance_cost / gencapmw AS mce, avg_rev_loss / gencapmw AS rlr FROM plant_maintenance_costs ) SELECT growalias, mce, rlr, rlr / mce AS mroi FROM maint_efficiency

question: Please identify the areas that need cleaning based on Cleaning Triggers by displaying the area ID, environmental readings measurement time, soiling loss percentage, dust density, and average soiling impact factor.
SQL: WITH soiling_data AS ( SELECT e.arearegistry, e.envmoment, e.soillosspct, e.dustdengm2, AVG(e.soillosspct / e.dustdengm2) OVER ( PARTITION BY e.arearegistry ) as avg_sif FROM environment e ), cleaning_schedule AS ( SELECT sd.arearegistry, sd.envmoment, sd.soillosspct, sd.dustdengm2, sd.avg_sif, LAG( sd.envmoment, 1, DATE(sd.envmoment, '-30 days') ) OVER ( PARTITION BY sd.arearegistry ORDER BY sd.envmoment ) as prev_moment FROM soiling_data sd ) SELECT cs.arearegistry, cs.envmoment, cs.soillosspct, cs.dustdengm2, cs.avg_sif FROM cleaning_schedule cs WHERE cs.soillosspct > 5 OR cs.dustdengm2 > 0.15 OR ( cs.avg_sif * cs.dustdengm2 ) > 0.15 OR JULIANDAY(cs.envmoment) - JULIANDAY(cs.prev_moment) > 30;
evidence: Soiling Impact Factor (SIF): Quantifies the impact of soiling on power production based on dust density., Soiling Cleaning Threshold: Defines when panel cleaning should be performed based on soiling conditions., Cleaning Triggers: Combined conditions that determine when solar panel cleaning is economically justified.

question: I want to compute Total System Loss (TSL) per solar panel using Inverter Efficiency Loss (IEL). Can you provide each panel ID with rated power, measured power, degradation loss, soiling loss, inverter loss and summarized TSL by summing these losses?
SQL: WITH inverter_loss AS ( SELECT p.solmodref, ROUND( p.measpoww * ( 1 - CAST(( i.power_metrics ->> '$.inverteffpct' ) AS REAL) / 100 ), 2 ) AS IEL FROM performance AS p INNER JOIN panel AS pa ON p.solmodref = pa.panemark INNER JOIN inverter AS i ON i.siteref = pa.hubregistry ) SELECT p.solmodref AS panel_id, pa.powratew AS rated_power, p.measpoww AS measured_power, ROUND( pa.powratew * ( CAST(( p.efficiency_profile -> '$.degradation' ->> '$.cumdegpct' ) AS REAL) / 100 ), 2 ) AS degradation_loss, ROUND(p.measpoww * ( env.soillosspct / 100.0 ), 2) AS soiling_loss, inv.IEL AS inverter_loss, ROUND( ( pa.powratew * ( CAST(( p.efficiency_profile -> '$.degradation' ->> '$.cumdegpct' ) AS REAL) / 100 ) ) + ( p.measpoww * ( env.soillosspct / 100.0 ) ) + inv.IEL, 2 ) AS TSL FROM performance AS p INNER JOIN panel AS pa ON p.solmodref = pa.panemark INNER JOIN environment AS env ON env.arearegistry = pa.hubregistry INNER JOIN inverter_loss AS inv ON inv.solmodref = p.solmodref
evidence: Inverter Efficiency Loss (IEL): Calculates the energy lost due to inverter inefficiency., Total System Loss (TSL): Calculates the combined power losses from all major sources., CumDegPct (Cumulative Degradation Percentage): Illustrates the total performance loss over a panel's lifetime.

question: Calculate Fill Factor Degradation Rate (FFDR) for solar panels. Output should include panel ID, initial fill factor, current fill factor, the number of years since installation and the FFDR. When computing FFDR, please ensure that division errors are avoided.
SQL: SELECT pa.panemark AS panel_id, elec.ffactorinit AS fill_factor_initial, elec.ffactorcurr AS fill_factor_current, CAST(strftime('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', plant.initdate) AS INTEGER) AS years_since_installation, ROUND(((elec.ffactorinit - elec.ffactorcurr) / NULLIF(CAST(strftime('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', plant.initdate) AS INTEGER), 0) * 100), 2) AS FFDR FROM electrical elec INNER JOIN panel pa ON elec.engyunitref = pa.panemark INNER JOIN plant ON pa.hubregistry = plant.growregistry;
evidence: Fill Factor Degradation Rate (FFDR): Calculates the rate at which the fill factor of a panel is degrading over time.

question: Determine Weather Corrected Efficiency (WCE) for solar panels, including panel ID, temperature coefficient, cell temperature, current efficiency, plane-of-array irradiance and the computed WCE, rounding to two decimal places.
SQL: SELECT p.solmodref AS panel_id, pa.tempcoef AS temperature_coefficient, env.celltempc AS cell_temperature, CAST(( p.efficiency_profile -> '$.current_efficiency' ->> '$.curreffpct' ) AS REAL) AS current_efficiency, CAST(( env.irradiance_conditions -> '$.irradiance_types' ->> '$[3]' ) AS REAL) AS poa_irradiance, ROUND( ( CAST(( p.efficiency_profile -> '$.current_efficiency' ->> '$.curreffpct' ) AS REAL) * ( 1 + pa.tempcoef * ( 25 - env.celltempc ) / 100 ) * ( 1000 / ( CAST(( env.irradiance_conditions -> '$.irradiance_types' ->> '$[3]' ) AS REAL) ) ) ), 2 ) AS WCE FROM performance AS p INNER JOIN panel AS pa ON p.solmodref = pa.panemark INNER JOIN environment AS env ON env.arearegistry = pa.hubregistry
evidence: Weather Corrected Efficiency (WCE): Adjusts panel efficiency measurements to account for weather conditions., TempCoef (Temperature Coefficient): Illustrates how panel performance changes with temperature., CellTempC (Cell Temperature): Illustrates the operating temperature of solar cells., POAIrradianceWM2 (Plane-of-Array Irradiance): Illustrates the solar energy available to panels in their installed orientation.

question: To assess degradation trends, please extract the plant name, panel ID, installation date, service years, initial and current efficiency, annual degradation rate, the Panel Efficiency Loss Rate (PELR), the calculated NDI and then categorize panels based on Degradation Severity Classification.
SQL: WITH panel_base_data AS ( SELECT p.panemark, p.hubregistry, p.paneeffpct AS initial_efficiency, plant.initdate AS installation_date, plant.growalias AS plant_name, CAST(strftime('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', plant.initdate) AS INTEGER) AS years_in_service FROM panel p JOIN plant ON p.hubregistry = plant.growregistry WHERE plant.initdate IS NOT NULL ), efficiency_data AS ( SELECT pbd.panemark, pbd.initial_efficiency, pbd.installation_date, pbd.plant_name, pbd.years_in_service, perf.perfmoment, REPLACE(REPLACE(JSON_EXTRACT(perf.efficiency_profile, '$.current_efficiency.curreffpct'), '[', ''), ']', '') AS current_efficiency, REPLACE(REPLACE(JSON_EXTRACT(perf.efficiency_profile, '$.degradation.anndegrate'), '[', ''), ']', '') AS annual_deg_rate, CAST(strftime('%Y', perf.perfmoment) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', pbd.installation_date) AS INTEGER) AS measurement_age_years, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY perf.solmodref ORDER BY perf.perfmoment DESC) AS rn FROM panel_base_data pbd JOIN performance perf ON pbd.panemark = perf.solmodref WHERE perf.efficiency_profile IS NOT NULL ), degradation_analysis AS ( SELECT ed.panemark, ed.initial_efficiency, ed.installation_date, ed.plant_name, ed.years_in_service, ed.current_efficiency, ed.annual_deg_rate, CASE WHEN ed.measurement_age_years > 0 THEN (ed.initial_efficiency - ed.current_efficiency) / ed.measurement_age_years ELSE NULL END AS pelr FROM efficiency_data ed WHERE ed.rn = 1 ), normalized_degradation AS ( SELECT da.panemark, da.initial_efficiency, da.installation_date, da.plant_name, da.years_in_service, da.current_efficiency, da.annual_deg_rate, da.pelr, CASE WHEN da.annual_deg_rate > 0 THEN da.pelr / da.annual_deg_rate ELSE NULL END AS ndi FROM degradation_analysis da ) SELECT nd.plant_name, nd.panemark AS panel_id, strftime('%Y-%m-%d', nd.installation_date) AS installation_date, nd.years_in_service, ROUND(nd.initial_efficiency, 2) AS initial_efficiency_pct, ROUND(nd.current_efficiency, 2) AS current_efficiency_pct, ROUND(nd.annual_deg_rate, 2) AS annual_degradation_rate_pct, ROUND(nd.pelr * 100, 2) AS panel_efficiency_loss_rate_pct, ROUND(nd.ndi, 2) AS normalized_degradation_index, CASE WHEN nd.ndi > 1.5 THEN 'High Degradation' WHEN nd.ndi > 1.0 THEN 'Moderate Degradation' ELSE 'Normal Degradation' END AS degradation_level FROM normalized_degradation nd;
evidence: Panel Efficiency Loss Rate (PELR): Calculates the percentage of efficiency loss per year for a solar panel., Normalized Degradation Index (NDI): Compares panel degradation to expected rates based on panel type and age., Degradation Severity Classification: Defines thresholds for high, moderate, and normal degradation based on NDI value., AnnDegRate (Annual Degradation Rate): Illustrates the yearly performance degradation of solar panels.

question: Show me the health status of all vaccine storage containers, including their ID, average Temperature Stability Score, maximum Temperature Breach Severity, and Container Health Status for the past 1 year. Round the scores to two decimals, include containers even if they have no sensor data, and limit to 100 containers.
SQL: SELECT c.containregistry, ROUND(AVG(s.tempstabidx), 2) AS avg_temp_stability_score, MAX(CASE WHEN s.alertkind = 'Temperature' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS max_temp_breach_severity, CASE WHEN AVG(s.tempstabidx) > 0.9 THEN 'Healthy' WHEN AVG(s.tempstabidx) > 0.7 THEN 'Needs Attention' ELSE 'Critical' END AS container_health_status FROM container AS c LEFT JOIN sensordata AS s ON c.containregistry = s.containlink WHERE s.alerttime >= date('now', '-1 year') OR s.alerttime IS NULL GROUP BY c.containregistry LIMIT 100;
evidence: Temperature Stability Score (TSS): Calculates the overall temperature stability of a container based on deviations and critical events., Container Risk Index (CRI): Calculates overall risk level for a container based on temperature stability and coolant status., Temperature Breach Severity (TBS): Calculates severity of temperature breaches., Container Health Status: Classifies containers based on overall risk and temperature stability to prioritize immediate action and monitor operational trends.

question: Show me the top 10 transport modes with the most reliable Stable Transport over the past 3 months. For each mode, list the mode name, average Handling Quality Index rounded to 3 decimal places, vehicles involved in Stable Transport, and the count of Stable Transport instances. Sort by average Handling Quality Index from highest to lowest, including only modes with positive handling quality.
SQL: WITH HandlingMetrics AS (SELECT t.VehicleReg, t.TransMode, (1.0 - COALESCE(s.HandleEvents / 100.0, 0)) * (1.0 - COALESCE(s.CritEvents / 10.0, 0)) AS HQI, COALESCE((1.0 - COALESCE(s.TempDevCount / 100.0, 0)) * (1.0 - COALESCE(s.CritEvents / 10.0, 0)) * COALESCE(s.TempStabIdx, 1.0), 1.0) AS TSS FROM TransportInfo AS t INNER JOIN SensorData AS s ON t.VehicleReg = s.VehSenseRef) SELECT TransMode, ROUND(AVG(HQI), 3) AS avg_hqi, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN HQI > 0.9 AND TSS > 0.8 THEN VehicleReg END, ',') AS vehicles, SUM(CASE WHEN HQI > 0.9 AND TSS > 0.8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS stable_transports FROM HandlingMetrics GROUP BY TransMode HAVING AVG(HQI) > 0 ORDER BY avg_hqi DESC LIMIT 10;
evidence: Temperature Stability Score (TSS): Calculates the overall temperature stability of a container based on deviations and critical events., Handling Quality Index (HQI): Measures quality of shipment handling., Stable Transport: Identifies stable transport conditions.

question: List the top 10 critical vaccine containers, sorted by risk rank from highest to lowest. Display each container's ID, maximum Temperature Stability Score and Container Risk Index (both rounded to 3 decimal places), Risk Rank, and sensor data availability status (classify as 'No Sensor Data' if the sensor data record is NULL and 'Sensor Data Available' otherwise). Include a diagnostic JSON summary containing the maximum temperature deviation count, maximum critical events, maximum temperature stability index, current coolant percentage remaining, and maximum temperature breach severity (use field names 'TempDevCount', 'CritEvents', 'TempStabIdx', 'CoolRemainPct', 'TempBreachSeverity'). Include all containers in the evaluation, even those without sensor data.
SQL: WITH StabilityMetrics AS ( SELECT c.containregistry, (1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.tempdevcount AS REAL) / 100, 0)) * (1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.critevents AS REAL) / 10, 0)) * COALESCE(s.tempstabidx, 1) AS TSS, COALESCE( ABS(s.tempnowc - s.storetempc) / NULLIF(s.temptolc, 0) * s.tempdevcount, 0 ) AS TBS, s.tempdevcount, s.critevents, s.tempstabidx, s.tempnowc, s.storetempc, s.temptolc, s.alerttime, CASE WHEN s.sensortrack IS NULL THEN 'No Sensor Data' ELSE 'Sensor Data Available' END AS SensorDataStatus FROM container c LEFT JOIN sensordata s ON c.containregistry = s.containlink WHERE s.alerttime IS NULL OR s.alerttime >= date('now', '-1 year') ), RiskIndex AS ( SELECT sm.containregistry, COALESCE(MAX(sm.TSS), 1.0) AS TSS, COALESCE(MAX(sm.TBS), 0.0) AS max_TBS, (1 - COALESCE(MAX(sm.TSS), 1.0)) * (1 - COALESCE(c.coolremainpct, 0) / 100) AS CRI, MAX(sm.SensorDataStatus) AS SensorDataStatus, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (1 - COALESCE(MAX(sm.TSS), 1.0)) * (1 - COALESCE(c.coolremainpct, 0) / 100) DESC) AS RiskRank, json_object( 'TempDevCount', MAX(sm.tempdevcount), 'CritEvents', MAX(sm.critevents), 'TempStabIdx', MAX(sm.tempstabidx), 'CoolRemainPct', c.coolremainpct, 'TempBreachSeverity', MAX(sm.TBS) ) AS DiagnosticInfo FROM StabilityMetrics sm LEFT JOIN container c ON sm.containregistry = c.containregistry GROUP BY sm.containregistry, c.coolremainpct ) SELECT containregistry, ROUND(TSS, 3) AS TSS, ROUND(CRI, 3) AS CRI, RiskRank, SensorDataStatus, DiagnosticInfo FROM RiskIndex WHERE CRI > 0.6 OR TSS < 0.4 ORDER BY RiskRank LIMIT 10
evidence: Temperature Stability Score (TSS): Calculates the overall temperature stability of a container based on deviations and critical events., Container Risk Index (CRI): Calculates overall risk level for a container based on temperature stability and coolant status., Temperature Breach Severity (TBS): Calculates severity of temperature breaches., Container Health Status: Classifies containers based on overall risk and temperature stability to prioritize immediate action and monitor operational trends., Risk Rank: Ranks containers based on their risk level.

question: For each transport route in the vaccine database, identify High-Risk Routes. For each vehicle, show the vehicle ID, shipment ID, Route Completion Percentage rounded to 3 decimal places, maximum Container Risk Index rounded to 3 decimal places, distance done in kilometers, distance left in kilometers, maximum temperature deviation count, maximum critical events, maximum temperature stability index, and maximum coolant remaining percentage. Sort by maximum Container Risk Index from highest to lowest and limit to 10 results.
SQL: WITH RouteProgress AS ( SELECT t.VehicleReg, t.ShipTransit, t.DistDoneKm, t.DistLeftKm, ( t.DistDoneKm / NULLIF(t.DistDoneKm + t.DistLeftKm, 0) ) * 100 AS RCP FROM TransportInfo AS t WHERE NOT t.DistDoneKm IS NULL AND NOT t.DistLeftKm IS NULL ), ContainerRisk AS ( SELECT c.ContainRegistry, c.ShipOwn, c.CoolRemainPct, ( 1 - ( ( 1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.TempDevCount AS REAL) / 100, 0) ) * ( 1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.CritEvents AS REAL) / 10, 0) ) * COALESCE(s.TempStabIdx, 1) ) ) * ( 1 - COALESCE(c.CoolRemainPct, 0) / 100 ) AS CRI, s.TempDevCount, s.CritEvents, s.TempStabIdx FROM Container AS c FULL JOIN SensorData AS s ON c.ContainRegistry = s.ContainLink WHERE NOT c.ShipOwn IS NULL OR NOT s.ContainLink IS NULL ) SELECT rp.VehicleReg AS vehicle_id, rp.ShipTransit AS shipment_id, ROUND(CAST(rp.RCP AS REAL), 3) AS rcp, COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(MAX(cr.CRI) AS REAL), 3), 0) AS max_cri, rp.DistDoneKm AS dist_done_km, rp.DistLeftKm AS dist_left_km, CAST(MAX(cr.TempDevCount) AS TEXT) AS temp_dev_count, CAST(MAX(cr.CritEvents) AS TEXT) AS crit_events, CAST(MAX(cr.TempStabIdx) AS TEXT) AS temp_stab_idx, CAST(MAX(cr.CoolRemainPct) AS TEXT) AS cool_remain_pct FROM RouteProgress AS rp LEFT JOIN ContainerRisk AS cr ON rp.ShipTransit = cr.ShipOwn WHERE rp.RCP < 50 GROUP BY rp.VehicleReg, rp.ShipTransit, rp.RCP, rp.DistDoneKm, rp.DistLeftKm HAVING MAX(cr.CRI) > 0.4 OR MAX(cr.CRI) IS NULL ORDER BY COALESCE(MAX(cr.CRI), 0) DESC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 10

question: Show me all Compromised Shipments, listing their shipment ID, risk status, number of incidents, and maintenance record IDs as an array. Only include shipments flagged as compromised, sort them by incident count from highest to lowest, and limit to 50 results.
SQL: WITH ShipmentRisk AS ( SELECT s.ShipmentRegistry, CASE WHEN s.IntegrityMark = 'Compromised' OR s.SealFlag = 'Broken' OR s.TamperSign = 'Confirmed' THEN 'Compromised' ELSE 'Safe' END AS risk_status, COALESCE(rm.Incidents, 0) AS incident_count FROM Shipments s LEFT JOIN RegulatoryAndMaintenance rm ON s.ShipmentRegistry = rm.ShipGov ) SELECT ShipmentRegistry, risk_status, incident_count, GROUP_CONCAT(rm.RegMaintRegistry) AS maintenance_ids FROM ShipmentRisk sr LEFT JOIN RegulatoryAndMaintenance rm ON sr.ShipmentRegistry = rm.ShipGov WHERE risk_status = 'Compromised' GROUP BY ShipmentRegistry, risk_status, incident_count ORDER BY incident_count DESC LIMIT 50

question: For each transport, I want to identify Stable Transports. Please list the vehicle ID, shipment ID, Handling Quality Index and Temperature Stability Score rounded to 3 decimal places, based on the most recent sensor reading. Sort by TSS from highest to lowest.
SQL: WITH TransportStability AS ( SELECT t.vehiclereg, t.shiptransit, (1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.HandleEvents AS REAL) / 100, 0)) * (1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.CritEvents AS REAL) / 10, 0)) AS HQI, (1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.TempDevCount AS REAL) / 100, 0)) * (1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.CritEvents AS REAL) / 10, 0)) * COALESCE(s.TempStabIdx, 1) AS TSS, s.AlertTime FROM TransportInfo t LEFT JOIN SensorData s ON t.vehiclereg = s.VehSenseRef WHERE s.sensortrack IN (SELECT sensortrack FROM SensorData WHERE VehSenseRef = t.vehiclereg ORDER BY AlertTime DESC LIMIT 1) ) SELECT vehiclereg, shiptransit, ROUND(HQI, 3) AS HQI, ROUND(TSS, 3) AS TSS FROM TransportStability WHERE HQI > 0.9 AND TSS > 0.8 ORDER BY TSS DESC
evidence: Temperature Stability Score (TSS): Calculates the overall temperature stability of a container based on deviations and critical events., Handling Quality Index (HQI): Measures quality of shipment handling., Stable Transport: Identifies stable transport conditions.

question: For each container, I want to identify those with a Temperature Alert. Please list the container ID, Temperature Breach Severity, number of temperature deviations, and an array of alert types for each sensor reading. Sort by TBS from highest to lowest and limit to 5 results.
SQL: SELECT c.ContainRegistry, CAST(ABS(s.TempNowC - s.StoreTempC) AS REAL) / NULLIF(s.TempTolC, 0) * s.TempDevCount AS TBS, s.TempDevCount, GROUP_CONCAT(s.AlertKind) AS AlertTypes FROM Container c INNER JOIN SensorData s ON c.ContainRegistry = s.ContainLink WHERE CAST(ABS(s.TempNowC - s.StoreTempC) AS REAL) / NULLIF(s.TempTolC, 0) * s.TempDevCount > 2.0 AND s.TempDevCount > 5 GROUP BY c.ContainRegistry, s.TempNowC, s.StoreTempC, s.TempTolC, s.TempDevCount ORDER BY TBS DESC LIMIT 5
evidence: Temperature Breach Severity (TBS): Calculates severity of temperature breaches., Temperature Alert: Identifies critical temperature conditions.

question: For each container, I want to identify those with a Coolant Critical condition. Please list the container ID, coolant remaining percentage, Coolant Depletion Rate rounded to 2 decimal places, and Depletion Rank based on CDR. Sort by Depletion Rank and limit to 5 results.
SQL: WITH CoolantStatus AS (SELECT c.ContainRegistry, c.CoolRemainPct, (100.0 - c.CoolRemainPct) / NULLIF(julianday('now') - julianday(c.RefillLatest), 0) AS CDR, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (100.0 - c.CoolRemainPct) / NULLIF(julianday('now') - julianday(c.RefillLatest), 0) DESC) AS DepletionRank FROM Container c WHERE c.RefillLatest IS NOT NULL) SELECT ContainRegistry, CoolRemainPct, ROUND(CDR, 2) AS CDR, DepletionRank FROM CoolantStatus WHERE CDR IS NOT NULL ORDER BY DepletionRank LIMIT 5
evidence: Coolant Depletion Rate (CDR): Measures how quickly the coolant is being depleted., Coolant Critical: Identifies critical coolant conditions., Depletion Rank: Ranks containers based on the rate of coolant depletion.

question: For each container, I want to identify those with an Efficient Container status. Please list the container ID, Storage Efficiency Ratio rounded to 2 decimal places, Temperature Stability Score rounded to 2 decimal places, and Efficiency Rank based on SER. Sort by Efficiency Rank and limit to 5 results.
SQL: WITH EfficiencyMetrics AS ( SELECT c.ContainRegistry, CAST(( v.VialTally * 10 ) AS REAL) / NULLIF(c.VolLiters, 0) AS SER, ( 1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.TempDevCount AS REAL) / 100, 0) ) * ( 1 - COALESCE(CAST(s.CritEvents AS REAL) / 10, 0) ) * COALESCE(s.TempStabIdx, 1) AS TSS, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY CAST(( v.VialTally * 10 ) AS REAL) / NULLIF(c.VolLiters, 0) DESC) AS EfficiencyRank FROM Container AS c FULL JOIN VaccineDetails AS v ON c.ContainRegistry = v.ContainVac INNER JOIN SensorData AS s ON c.ContainRegistry = s.ContainLink ) SELECT ContainRegistry, ROUND(CAST(SER AS REAL), 2) AS SER, ROUND(CAST(TSS AS REAL), 2) AS TSS, EfficiencyRank FROM EfficiencyMetrics WHERE SER > 0.8 AND TSS > 0.9 ORDER BY EfficiencyRank NULLS LAST LIMIT 5
evidence: Temperature Stability Score (TSS): Calculates the overall temperature stability of a container based on deviations and critical events., Storage Efficiency Ratio (SER): Measures how efficiently container volume is utilized., Efficient Container: Identifies efficiently utilized containers., Efficiency Rank: Ranks containers based on their storage efficiency.

question: List 5 equipments overdue for maintenance in the vaccine database, based on Maintenance Due status. For each, show the equipment ID, Maintenance Compliance Score rounded to 2 decimal places, the number of Days Overdue as an integer, and its maintenance status 'Overdue'. Sort by Days Overdue from longest to shortest, including only equipment with valid compliance scores.
SQL: WITH MaintenanceStatus AS ( SELECT rm.RegMaintRegistry, rm.CompScore, rm.Incidents, rm.MaintDateNext, rm.CalibDateNext, COALESCE(rm.CompScore * (1 - COALESCE(rm.Incidents, 0) / 10), 0) AS MCS FROM RegulatoryAndMaintenance rm ) SELECT RegMaintRegistry, ROUND(MCS, 2) AS mcs, MAX( ( JULIANDAY(date('now')) - JULIANDAY(MaintDateNext) ), ( JULIANDAY(date('now')) - JULIANDAY(CalibDateNext) ), 0 ) AS days_overdue, 'Overdue' AS maintenance_status FROM MaintenanceStatus WHERE MCS < 0.7 AND (date('now') > MaintDateNext OR date('now') > CalibDateNext) AND MCS IS NOT NULL ORDER BY days_overdue DESC LIMIT 5
evidence: Maintenance Compliance Score (MCS): Calculates compliance with maintenance schedules., Maintenance Due: Identifies equipment requiring maintenance., Days Overdue: Calculates the number of days past the scheduled maintenance or calibration date.

question: I want to identify all free and basic tier members who show traits of being Gift-Focused Supporters. Please list their user IDs, nicknames, Gift Impact Quotient (rounded to 2 decimal places), and current membership type, sorted by Gift Impact Quotient in descending order.
SQL: WITH gift_metrics AS ( SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, i.giftvalusd, i.gifttot, ( i.giftvalusd * i.gifttot / 100.0 ) AS gift_impact_quotient, ms.spendusd, ms.membkind FROM fans AS f JOIN interactions AS i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry JOIN membershipandspending AS ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry ) SELECT userregistry, nicklabel, ROUND(gift_impact_quotient, 2) AS giq, membkind FROM gift_metrics WHERE gift_impact_quotient > 50 AND spendusd < 100 AND membkind IN ('Free', 'Basic') ORDER BY gift_impact_quotient DESC NULLS FIRST
evidence: Gift Impact Quotient (GIQ): Evaluates the relative impact of a fan's gifting behavior considering both volume and value, Gift-Focused Supporter: Identifies fans whose primary support comes through gifting rather than direct spending, interactions.gifttot_interactions.giftvalusd: Explains the statistical significance of gift quantity and value

question: Find all Superfans in our database and display their nicknames, tier levels, Fan Engagement Index, and Monetization Value. Indicate which ones qualify as true Superfans based on the Superfan criteria and label them as 'Superfan', otherwise label them as 'Regular Fan'. Please sort the results by highest engagement first, then by monetary value in descending order. Only consider fans with active and VIP status.
SQL: SELECT f.nicklabel, f.tierstep, ROUND( CAST(( e.engrate * 0.4 + e.socintscore / 100 * 0.3 + e.actdayswk / 7.0 * 0.2 + e.avgsesscount / 10.0 * 0.1 ) AS REAL), 2 ) AS fei, ROUND(CAST(( ms.spendusd * ( 1 + ms.membdays / 365.0 * 0.5 ) ) AS REAL), 2) AS mv, CASE WHEN f.tierstep >= 8 AND ( e.engrate * 0.4 + e.socintscore / 100 * 0.3 + e.actdayswk / 7.0 * 0.2 + e.avgsesscount / 10.0 * 0.1 ) > 0.7 AND ms.spendusd * ( 1 + ms.membdays / 365.0 * 0.5 ) > 200 THEN 'Superfan' ELSE 'Regular Fan' END AS fan_classification FROM fans AS f JOIN membershipandspending AS ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry JOIN engagement AS e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg WHERE f.statustag = 'Active' OR f.statustag = 'VIP' ORDER BY fei DESC NULLS FIRST, mv DESC NULLS FIRST
evidence: Superfan: Identifies fans with exceptional platform value and engagement, fans.tierstep: Explains the practical significance of fan tier levels, Fan Engagement Index (FEI): A comprehensive metric measuring fan activity level with platform and virtual idols, Monetization Value (MV): Calculates the monetary value a fan brings to the platform over time

question: Can you recognize all Whale fans in our system? I need a list showing their user ID, nickname, and total financial support in USD (combining both direct spending and gift values). Sort the results by total support amount from highest to lowest. Need to consider all fans who may not have interaction records in our system yet.
SQL: SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, (COALESCE(ms.spendusd, 0) + COALESCE(i.giftvalusd, 0)) AS total_support_usd FROM fans f LEFT JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry LEFT JOIN interactions i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry WHERE COALESCE(i.giftvalusd, 0) + COALESCE(ms.spendusd, 0) > 0 ORDER BY total_support_usd DESC;
evidence: Whale: Identifies fans who provide extraordinary financial support, interactions.gifttot_interactions.giftvalusd: Explains the statistical significance of gift quantity and value

question: Show me a breakdown of our fan base using the tierstep classification system. I need to see each tier category, the count of fans in each category, their average points, and average spending amounts. All the calculations should be rounded to 2 decimal places. Include all fans with Active or VIP status, and make sure to include data from fans who may not have spending records in our system yet.
SQL: WITH tiered_fans AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN f.tierstep BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN 'Entry-level' WHEN f.tierstep BETWEEN 4 AND 7 THEN 'Mid-level' WHEN f.tierstep BETWEEN 8 AND 10 THEN 'High-level' WHEN f.tierstep > 10 THEN 'Core' ELSE 'Undefined' END AS tier_category, f.ptsval, COALESCE(ms.spendusd, 0) AS spendusd FROM fans AS f LEFT JOIN membershipandspending AS ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry WHERE f.statustag IN ('Active', 'VIP') ) SELECT tier_category, COUNT(*) AS fan_count, ROUND(AVG(ptsval), 2) AS avg_points, ROUND(AVG(spendusd), 2) AS avg_spending FROM tiered_fans GROUP BY 1

question: Please identify users who qualify as Content Creator Classification by showing their user ID, nickname, content quality score, content volume, follower count, and Content Creator Classification. Could you sort the results by content quality first, then by follower count - both in descending order?
SQL: SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.contqualrate' ) AS REAL) AS content_quality, CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.ugcval' ) AS INTEGER) AS content_volume, CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.network' ->> '$.follcount' ) AS INTEGER) AS follower_count, CASE WHEN CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.contqualrate' ) AS REAL) > 8.5 AND CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.network' ->> '$.follcount' ) AS INTEGER) > 1000 AND CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.ugcval' ) AS INTEGER) > 20 THEN 'High-Value Content Creator' WHEN CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.contqualrate' ) AS REAL) > 7.0 AND CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.ugcval' ) AS INTEGER) > 20 THEN 'Content Creator' ELSE 'Regular Fan' END AS creator_classification FROM fans AS f JOIN membershipandspending AS ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry JOIN engagement AS e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg JOIN socialcommunity AS sc ON sc.socialengagepivot = e.engagereg WHERE NOT CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.contqualrate' ) AS REAL) IS NULL ORDER BY content_quality DESC NULLS FIRST, follower_count DESC NULLS FIRST
evidence: Content Creator Classification: Categorizes fans based on their content creation quality, volume, and reach, socialcommunity.community_engagement.content_creation.contqualrate: Explains content quality rating standards and classification, Content Creator: Identifies fans who actively produce and share idol-related content, High-Value Content Creator: Identifies fans who produce exceptional quality content with significant reach

SQL: WITH fan_memberships AS ( SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, ms.memberreg, ms.spendusd, ms.membdays, ms.membkind FROM fans AS f JOIN membershipandspending AS ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry ), fan_interactions AS ( SELECT i.interactfanpivot AS userregistry, i.gifttot, CAST(( i.engagement_metrics -> '$.chat_activity' ->> '$.chatmsg' ) AS INTEGER) AS chatmsg, CAST(( i.engagement_metrics -> '$.session' ->> '$.watchhrs' ) AS REAL) AS watch_hours FROM interactions AS i ), silent_supporters AS ( SELECT fm.userregistry, fm.nicklabel, fm.spendusd * ( 1 + fm.membdays / 365.0 * 0.5 ) * ( 1 + COALESCE(fi.gifttot, 0) / 10.0 * 0.2 ) AS mv, e.engrate, fi.chatmsg, p.sesscount, CAST(COALESCE(fi.chatmsg, 0) AS REAL) / NULLIF(p.sesscount, 0) AS chat_message_ratio, e.contpref, fm.membkind, fm.membdays, fm.spendusd, fi.watch_hours FROM fan_memberships AS fm JOIN engagement AS e ON e.engagememberpivot = fm.memberreg LEFT JOIN fan_interactions AS fi ON fi.userregistry = fm.userregistry JOIN preferencesandsettings AS p ON p.preferencesmemberpivot = fm.memberreg WHERE fm.spendusd * ( 1 + fm.membdays / 365.0 * 0.5 ) * ( 1 + COALESCE(fi.gifttot, 0) / 10.0 * 0.2 ) > 100 AND e.engrate < 0.3 AND CAST(COALESCE(fi.chatmsg, 0) AS REAL) / NULLIF(p.sesscount, 0) < 0.5 ) SELECT nicklabel, mv, engrate, chat_message_ratio, membkind, spendusd / NULLIF(watch_hours, 0) AS revenue_per_hour, CASE WHEN contpref = 'Music' THEN 'Content Consumer (Music)' WHEN contpref = 'Dance' THEN 'Content Consumer (Dance)' WHEN contpref = 'Gaming' THEN 'Content Consumer (Gaming)' ELSE 'General Content Consumer' END AS viewer_category FROM silent_supporters ORDER BY mv DESC NULLS FIRST
evidence: Silent Supporter: Identifies financially supportive fans with low social visibility, Content Preference Classification: Categorizes fans based on their primary content consumption preferences, engagement.engrate: Explains the calculation basis and business significance of fan engagement rate, Monetization Value (MV): Calculates the monetary value a fan brings to the platform over time

question: Give me a breakdown of fans by their churn risk level, showing the count of fans in each category, the average days since their last login, their average engagement rates, average interaction consistency, and a calculated average Retention Risk Factor for each group. All the calculations should be rounded to 2 decimal places. This will help me prioritize our retention strategies for different risk segments.
SQL: SELECT r.churnflag, COUNT(*) AS fan_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(CURRENT_DATE - p.lastlogdt) AS REAL), 2) AS avg_days_since_login, ROUND(CAST(AVG(e.engrate) AS REAL), 2) AS avg_engagement_rate, ROUND(CAST(AVG(p.intconsist) AS REAL), 2) AS avg_interaction_consistency, ROUND( CAST(AVG( ( 1 - p.intconsist ) * 2 + ( CURRENT_DATE - p.lastlogdt ) / 30.0 * 0.5 + CASE WHEN r.churnflag = 'None' THEN 0 WHEN r.churnflag = 'Low' THEN 1 WHEN r.churnflag = 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN r.churnflag = 'High' THEN 3 END ) AS REAL), 2 ) AS avg_retention_risk_factor FROM fans AS f JOIN membershipandspending AS ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry JOIN engagement AS e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg JOIN retentionandinfluence AS r ON r.retainengagepivot = e.engagereg JOIN preferencesandsettings AS p ON p.preferencesmemberpivot = ms.memberreg GROUP BY r.churnflag

question: Provide me with each fan's id, nickname, their calculated FLV value (rounded to 2 decimals), and classify them based on Fan Value Segmentation. Please sort the results by FLV in descending order.
SQL: WITH fan_memberships AS ( SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, ms.memberreg, ms.spendusd, ms.membdays, COALESCE(i.gifttot, 0) AS gifttot FROM fans f JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry LEFT JOIN interactions i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry ), fan_engagement AS ( SELECT fm.userregistry, fm.nicklabel, e.engrate * 0.4 + e.socintscore / 100 * 0.3 + e.actdayswk / 7.0 * 0.2 + e.avgsesscount / 10.0 * 0.1 AS fei, fm.spendusd * (1 + fm.membdays / 365.0 * 0.5) * (1 + fm.gifttot / 10.0 * 0.2) AS mv, e.engagereg FROM fan_memberships fm JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = fm.memberreg ), retention_risk AS ( SELECT fe.userregistry, fe.nicklabel, fe.fei, fe.mv, CASE WHEN r.churnflag = 'None' THEN 0 WHEN r.churnflag = 'Low' THEN 1 WHEN r.churnflag = 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN r.churnflag = 'High' THEN 3 END AS rrf_approx FROM fan_engagement fe JOIN retentionandinfluence r ON r.retainengagepivot = fe.engagereg ), fan_lifetime_value AS ( SELECT userregistry, nicklabel, mv * (1 - rrf_approx / 10.0) * (1 + fei) * 24 AS flv FROM retention_risk ), percentile_values AS ( SELECT (SELECT flv FROM fan_lifetime_value ORDER BY flv LIMIT 1 OFFSET (SELECT COUNT(*) * CAST((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fan_lifetime_value) * 0.5 AS INT))) AS median, (SELECT flv FROM fan_lifetime_value ORDER BY flv LIMIT 1 OFFSET (SELECT COUNT(*) * CAST((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fan_lifetime_value) * 0.75 AS INT))) AS p75, (SELECT flv FROM fan_lifetime_value ORDER BY flv LIMIT 1 OFFSET (SELECT COUNT(*) * CAST((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fan_lifetime_value) * 0.9 AS INT))) AS p90 FROM fan_lifetime_value ) SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, ROUND(f.flv, 2) AS flv, CASE WHEN f.flv > p.p90 THEN 'Top Tier' WHEN f.flv > p.p75 THEN 'High Value' WHEN f.flv > p.median THEN 'Medium Value' ELSE 'Low Value' END AS value_segment FROM fan_lifetime_value f, percentile_values p ORDER BY f.flv DESC;
evidence: Fan Engagement Index (FEI): A comprehensive metric measuring fan activity level with platform and virtual idols, Monetization Value (MV): Calculates the monetary value a fan brings to the platform over time, Fan Lifetime Value (FLV): Projects the total economic value of a fan throughout their relationship with the platform, Churn Risk Numeric Mapping: Converts the churn risk enum values to numeric form for analytical calculations, Fan Value Segmentation: Classifies fans into value tiers based on their Fan Lifetime Value (FLV) relative to platform-wide percentiles, Retention Risk Factor (RRF): Quantifies the risk of fan churn based on multiple behavioral indicators, retentionandinfluence.churnflag: Explains the judgment basis for churn risk rating

question: I need to identify our Community Pillars for upcoming platform development discussions. Show me a list of our community leaders with their nicknames, calculated Community Contribution Index scores rounded to two decimal places, their group roles, activity frequency, and membership duration in days. Only include fans who meet all the Community Pillar criteria. Sort the results by CCI score in descending order.
SQL: WITH fan_memberships AS ( SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, ms.memberreg, ms.membdays FROM fans AS f JOIN membershipandspending AS ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry ), fan_engagement AS ( SELECT fm.userregistry, fm.nicklabel, fm.membdays, e.engagereg, e.engrate, e.socintscore, e.actdayswk, e.avgsesscount, e.actfreq, e.engrate * 0.4 + e.socintscore / 100 * 0.3 + e.actdayswk / 7.0 * 0.2 + e.avgsesscount / 10.0 * 0.1 AS fei_approx FROM fan_memberships AS fm JOIN engagement AS e ON e.engagememberpivot = fm.memberreg ), community_data AS ( SELECT fe.userregistry, fe.nicklabel, fe.membdays, fe.actfreq, fe.fei_approx, sc.collabcount, sc.community_engagement, CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.group_involvement' ->> '$.grprole' ) AS TEXT) AS group_role, CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.contqualrate' ) AS REAL) AS contqualrate, CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.content_creation' ->> '$.ugcval' ) AS REAL) AS ugcval, CAST(( sc.community_engagement -> '$.network' ->> '$.follcount' ) AS REAL) AS follcount, ri.viralcont FROM fan_engagement AS fe JOIN socialcommunity AS sc ON sc.socialengagepivot = fe.engagereg JOIN retentionandinfluence AS ri ON ri.retainengagepivot = fe.engagereg ), cci_components AS ( SELECT cd.userregistry, cd.nicklabel, cd.contqualrate * ( cd.ugcval / 10.0 ) * ( 1 + cd.follcount / 100 * 0.5 ) AS ccis_approx, ( cd.follcount / 100 ) * ( fe.engrate * 2 ) * ( COALESCE(cd.viralcont, 0) + 1 ) * 0.5 AS sim_approx, cd.collabcount, cd.fei_approx, cd.actfreq, cd.membdays, cd.group_role FROM community_data AS cd JOIN fan_engagement AS fe ON fe.userregistry = cd.userregistry ) SELECT nicklabel, ROUND( CAST(( ccis_approx * 0.4 + sim_approx * 0.3 + collabcount * 0.1 + fei_approx * 0.2 ) AS REAL), 2 ) AS cci, group_role, actfreq, membdays FROM cci_components WHERE ( ccis_approx * 0.4 + sim_approx * 0.3 + collabcount * 0.1 + fei_approx * 0.2 ) > 7 AND actfreq = 'Daily' AND membdays > 180 AND ( group_role = 'Moderator' OR group_role = 'Leader' ) ORDER BY cci DESC NULLS FIRST
evidence: Fan Engagement Index (FEI): A comprehensive metric measuring fan activity level with platform and virtual idols, Content Creation Impact Score (CCIS): Measures the impact of fan-created content on the community, Social Influence Multiplier (SIM): Calculates how much a fan amplifies content through their social network, Community Contribution Index (CCI): Measures a fan's overall contribution to the virtual idol community, Community Pillar: Identifies fans who form the foundation of the idol community

question: Show me a list of fans with their user ID, nicknames, how many different idols they support, the names of these idols in array, and their average engagement rate rounded to 2 decimal places. Only include fans who are classified as Multi-Idol Supporters. Sort the results first by the number of idols supported (highest first), then by engagement rate (highest first).
SQL: SELECT f.userregistry, f.nicklabel, COUNT(DISTINCT i.interactidolpivot) AS idols_supported, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT vi.nametag) AS idol_names, ROUND(AVG(e.engrate), 2) AS avg_engagement_rate FROM fans f JOIN interactions i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry JOIN virtualidols vi ON vi.entityreg = i.interactidolpivot JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg WHERE e.engrate > 0.4 GROUP BY f.userregistry, f.nicklabel HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT i.interactidolpivot) >= 2 ORDER BY idols_supported DESC, avg_engagement_rate DESC;
